title: P2.15b Bound live board poll lifecycle
description: Objective: make every affordance-board poll deadline- and unmount-bounded while projecting transport health honestly. Deliverable: createBoardFeed owns and aborts one in-flight poll per generation, automatically retries only after bounded settlement, classifies successful SURFACE as CONNECTED, delivered REFUSED/UNREADABLE as LAGGING, and undelivered as DISCONNECTED while preserving safe daemon code/layer detail. Not in scope: runtime bootstrap/pairing, React shell ownership, retry controls, goal mutation, or foreign Control Room files. Exact verification: `pnpm exec vitest run apps/control-room/src/live/live-board.test.tsx` with exit 0 and nonzero Test Files/Tests lines.
definitionOfDone: Current-byte measurement confirms the default post has AbortSignal.timeout and a generation guard, but injected posts are unbounded and stop/unmount does not abort the active request.

Each poll generation owns an AbortController composed with requestTimeoutMs defaulting to 15000; both default and injected post paths receive that signal, and stop clears the timer/schedule and aborts the active request exactly once.

A hung poll settles as DISCONNECTED/UNDELIVERED with exact TRANSPORT_REQUEST_FAILED and schedules one retry; stop suppresses its abort frame, a late ignored response cannot reschedule, and restart creates exactly one fresh loop.

frameOfSurface projects SURFACE as CONNECTED, a delivered daemon REFUSED or malformed/unreadable answer as LAGGING rather than stale ONLINE or DISCONNECTED, and preserves validated daemon code/layer values in deterministic non-secret detail when supplied.

Focused tests cover success, timeout, explicit stop abort, restart/reconnect, feed loss, delivered refusal, unreadable body, and late response; nonzero mutation drills removing active abort, deadline racing, generation guard, or LAGGING classification red named assertions, and the exact verification command exits 0.
taskRails: Do not label a delivered daemon refusal as a transport failure, and do not label a timed-out/undelivered request as connected.
At most one request and one scheduled retry may belong to a running generation; stop/unmount must release both.

frameOfSurface: (1) carries a daemon refusal as LAGGING with its exact code and refusing layer; (2) never echoes a hostile or unbounded refusal token into the frame detail; (3) refuses an unreadable body with the stable code, as LAGGING not disconnected; (4) reports CONNECTED only for a valid SURFACE and never invents a transport verdict; (5) refuses an incomplete or partially malformed surface instead of hiding records.
createBoardFeed: (6) reports a DELIVERED answer whose body is not JSON as unreadable, not disconnected; (7) reports a delivered daemon refusal as LAGGING carrying its code and layer; (8) bounds an INJECTED post that hangs and re-arms exactly once; (9) bounds a DELIVERED response whose body never finishes reading; (10) aborts the in-flight request on stop without emitting a frame or re-arming; (11) consumes a response that arrives after its deadline instead of replaying it; (12) gives a restart its own request, drops the stopped one, then reports loss honestly.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the bounded lifecycle in `live-board-feed.ts`: widen SurfaceFrame.connection to include LAGGING; make frameOfSurface return CONNECTED only for a valid SURFACE, LAGGING for delivered REFUSED/malformed/unreadable/unknown answers, and DISCONNECTED only for undelivered transport. Preserve only conservative bounded uppercase daemon code/layer tokens in REFUSED detail, otherwise use LIVE_SURFACE_UNREADABLE. Change injected/default post to receive a signal. For each poll create one AbortController and clearable validated deadline, race the entire post plus JSON read against abort, pass the signal to ambient fetch, consume late settlement, and clear timer/listeners/active ownership in finally. On timeout while the generation is live emit exact DISCONNECTED/UNDELIVERED/TRANSPORT_REQUEST_FAILED and schedule once; on stop set running false/increment generation, cancel schedule and abort the active controller so the completion is suppressed. Keep start idempotent and one request/one schedule maximum, then rerun the owned describe gate green.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN. `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room exec vitest run src/live/live-board.test.tsx -t 'frameOfSurface|createBoardFeed'` EXIT=0, Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 16 passed | 6 skipped (22). All 12 step-1 reds cleared; the 4 pre-existing arms stayed green.

Implemented in live-board-feed.ts (292 lines, under the 400 split threshold; over the 250 target but taskRail 1 forbids a third file, so no split was available):
- SurfaceFrame.connection widened to "CONNECTED" | "DISCONNECTED" | "LAGGING". Verified consumer-safe: ConnectionState in v2/shell/shell-model.ts already carries LAGGING, and every other consumer (v2/goals/goal-model.ts:197, v2/goals/live-goals.tsx:42, v2/goals/work-board.tsx:123, live/live-app.tsx:41/58, live/live-board.tsx:98) gates on DISCONNECTED or outcome !== "SURFACE", so a LAGGING REFUSED/UNREADABLE frame still renders its refusal state with an empty offers array; no dispatch surface is enabled by the new state.
- frameOfSurface: CONNECTED only for a valid SURFACE; delivered REFUSED and every unreadable/unknown/malformed answer are LAGGING; DISCONNECTED can no longer be produced by the reader at all.
- refusalDetail(): SAFE_TOKEN = /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$/u gates both code and layer; detail is `${code} @ ${layer}` (the existing repo convention from live-dispatch.ts:426 and live-command-dispatch.ts:109), code alone when layer is absent/unsafe, LIVE_SURFACE_UNREADABLE when code is unsafe. Free text, lowercase, unbounded strings and non-strings never reach the operator surface.
- BoardFeedOptions.post is now (body: string, signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<Response>, non-optional signal. The default post hands that same signal to fetch instead of owning AbortSignal.timeout, so injected and ambient transports obey one bound.
- Per poll: one AbortController + one clearable setTimeout at deadlineOf(requestTimeoutMs) (default 15000; non-finite, <=0 and >2147483647 all fall back to the default, so no zero-delay busy retry and no ~1ms clamp). Promise.race([answer(signal), abortedBy(signal)]) covers the round trip AND the response.json() read, so a stalled body is bounded too; Promise.race subscribes to both inputs so a late settlement of either is consumed, never unhandled.
- finally clears the timer and releases active ownership only if the controller still owns the slot. Timeout emits DISCONNECTED/UNDELIVERED/TRANSPORT_REQUEST_FAILED and re-arms once, guarded by (!running || run !== generation).
- stop(): running=false and generation+=1 BEFORE aborting, then cancels the schedule and aborts the in-flight controller exactly once (active nulled before abort, so a second stop cannot re-abort). The abort's rejection lands in a generation that is already dead, so no teardown frame and no reschedule.

Adversarial findings and what I did about each:
- FIXED (test added): start() idempotence was untested. The stop arm now calls start() twice and asserts signals stays length 1 — one request per running generation, as taskRail 3 requires.
- FIXED (test added): deadlineOf() range validation was untested. New arm "falls back to the default deadline rather than firing on an unusable one" sweeps requestTimeoutMs 0, -1, NaN, Infinity and 2_147_483_648 and requires no frame and no reschedule within two macrotask turns. Drill (f) proves it reds.
- FIXED (test added): LAGGING carries actionsEnabled:true in v2/shell/shell-model.ts, so a LAGGING frame must not be dispatchable. New arm "never offers a dispatchable command on a LAGGING frame" drives a refusal, an unknown outcome and a malformed SURFACE through the feed and asserts offers and steps are both empty on all three.
- CHECKED, safe: parallel polls. active is overwritten only by a newer poll and the finally releases the slot only when the controller still owns it, so a stopped generation's poll cannot null a live one's controller.
- CHECKED, safe: timer leak. clearTimeout runs in finally on every exit; the race is guaranteed to settle because the deadline always aborts, and the deadline itself is range-clamped.
- CHECKED, safe: listener accumulation. abortedBy uses { once: true } and the controller/signal are per-poll, so nothing outlives its request.
- CHECKED, safe: raw reason leakage. The catch discards the abort/transport error entirely and emits the fixed TRANSPORT_REQUEST_FAILED literal; signal.reason is never read into detail. frameOfSurface only ever emits fixed literals or SAFE_TOKEN-validated code/layer, and the pass-through `outcome` is only reached on an exact "REFUSED"/"SURFACE" equality, so an unbounded outcome string cannot ride into a frame.
- CHECKED, safe: a throwing getter or a non-Response body. frameOfSurface is inside the same try as response.json(), so a throw on either becomes LAGGING/UNREADABLE, never a false DISCONNECTED.
- CHECKED, safe: SAFE_TOKEN /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$/u is linear with a bounded quantifier; no catastrophic backtracking on a huge input.
- NOTED, out of scope (pre-existing, unchanged by this diff): an onFrame callback that throws stops the loop from re-arming, and intervalMs is not range-validated. Both predate this task and neither is named in the DoD; fixing intervalMs would also change the schedule contract this task's rails fence off.
